text:
Maria Chen: Quick thread — proposal for probabilistic hedging + capacity-aware fallback inside the router. Trying to avoid a big canary infra refactor. High-level goal: keep router mostly stateless, rely on resiliency layer for enforcement, but let router nudge traffic based on capacity/cost. Thoughts?

Jonathan Park: Like the idea. Main tradeoff is determinism vs noise in metrics. Randomized routing avoids hard cutoff thundering herd but makes regression detection harder. We should use a per-session sticky hash so users see consistent behavior (and metrics can be grouped). @Maria, do you want stable seed per-deployment?

Lee Gomez: +1 on sticky. Also add a cost signal into the decision. Some fallbacks (quantized models, distill variants) have lower latency but higher token-cost due to repeated prompting. We need a budget-aware cap, not just latency/capacity.

Ashley Rivera: Observability requirements: every decision needs labels: policy, probability, draw_value, capacity_snapshot, cost_estimate, route_version. We should sample request+response bodies for ~0.1% of fallback events for quality checks. Also need SLO bucketing so we can detect user-impacted regressions quickly.

Maria Chen: Sketch of config I had in mind:
```yaml
policy: probabilistic_hedging
seed: deployment_id
sticky_key: session_id
base_prob: 0.05 # default prob to shadow/fallback
capacity_threshold_pct: 0.25 # when pool available fraction drops below this, scale up prob
max_prob: 0.5
cost_budget_per_minute: 1000  # token-cost units per tenant (soft limit)
ramp_window_secs: 300
metrics_labels: [decision_policy, draw, capacity_pct, cost_estimate]
```
This keeps config declarative so Dedicated/Private can tune independently.

Jonathan Park: Router responsibilities (proposal):
- compute routing decision + reason metadata (attach headers)
- perform sticky hashing (stateless: hash(session_id||seed))
- call resilience-proxy with annotated request (proxy applies circuits/retries)
- annotate trace/span with model-catalog alias used
Keep the router stateless to preserve scale and simplify failover.

Lee Gomez: Resilience-proxy needs to subscribe to capacity telemetry from dedicated pool manager (and a fallback-cost estimator service). If capacity < 20% then increase fallback prob with a linear ramp: prob = base_prob + (1 - capacity_pct/threshold)*scale, capped at max_prob. Also expose a probe endpoint for simulated routing decisions so we can run dry-runs.

Ashley Rivera: Telemetry fields (formalized):
- decision_policy (string)
- random_draw (0..1)
- draw_seed (int)
- capacity_snapshot {pool_id: pct_available} (stringified map)
- cost_estimate_tokens (int)
- route_version (string)
- sample_payload_id (uuid)
We should add these to spans + logs AND to per-model daily rollups.

deploy-bot: CI for branch "fallback-proto" passed. Canary deploy scheduled to eng-platform tomorrow 09:30 PT :rocket:

ops-bot: Heads up — running a short synthetic test after canary to validate routing stability and metric variance. Will post results in #eng-sre.

Maria Chen: Action items: 1) Jonathan -> draft router API surface + example headers (due Wed) 2) Lee -> capacity & cost signal spec + probe endpoint contract (due Thu) 3) Ashley -> telemetry schema + dashboard mocks (due Fri) 4) Maria -> prototype config+sim + small perf test against dedicated pool (end of week).

Jonathan Park: Ack. I'll open a draft RFC and include a small sim harness with deterministic seeding so we can reproduce metric noise.

Lee Gomez: I'll add the probe endpoint to the pool manager PR and include an export for instantaneous capacity_pct.

Ashley Rivera: I'll sketch dashboards and alert rules (regressions by cohort, fallback-usage vs error-rate).

Maria Chen: Thanks all. If we agree on scope I'll spin the RFC into a PR today. :+1:
